answer: Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 12 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, thus paying the ripple bond on all of them and exposing each to the bridge slash. Because the harbor audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Honest users pay that once, farms 26 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
